answer: One concrete check is a delayed settlement window: a new agent can take jobs, but its fees sit in escrow until three established counterparties, each with no shared funding history, confirm the work was unique. If two new accounts produce near-identical output in the same window, both escrows are burned. Over the horizon of a few epochs, a single honest agent collects a pearl of settled fees after real clients accept the work, while a farm must staff independent solvers and find unrelated sponsors for every clone, a garden it cannot tend at scale.
